target.title: refactor(gateway): trim session utils exports
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/gateway/session-utils.ts` still re-exported transcript readers, archive helpers, model identity helpers, support types, and internal projection functions that have no production consumer through that module. Those unsupported exports widened a legacy barrel and required 29 dead-code baseline entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change removes the unused forwarding exports, makes six session projection helpers/types module-private, moves the remaining transcript reader consumer to its canonical owner, and ratchets that import boundary. Tests now cover private behavior through `buildGatewaySessionRow`, keep model identity tests with `session-model-ref.ts`, and mock the canonical transcript reader module.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The gateway session projection and MCP reconstruction behavior are unchanged; the internal TypeScript surface is narrower and the dead-export baseline is smaller.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcd7rd6wga7karhs7wkbwdn`: 506 focused assertions passed across session model, gateway session, MCP reconstruction, chat history, and boundary suites.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports`: passed with the Knip baseline matching 5,863 entries.
- `pnpm check:changed -- <9 touched files>`: passed core, core-test, root-test, tooling, typecheck, formatting, lint, import-cycle, and database-first lanes.
- `node scripts/check-session-transcript-reader-boundary.mjs`: passed.
- Fresh post-fix dirty-tree `gpt-5.6-sol` medium autoreview: clean, confidence `0.96`.
- Fresh exact-commit `gpt-5.6-sol` medium autoreview: clean, confidence `0.94`.
- Full open-PR and target-symbol overlap audit found no competing cleanup.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Changelog: not required for an internal export and test-ownership cleanup.
